english.title: Driver / operator / manager fail to stop smoking in smoke-free vehicle used for work - Wales
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being

(A)_[the driver]_
(B)_[the operator]_
(C)_[a person concerned in the management]_

of a vehicle, namely **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE..), which, in accordance with regulation 15(3) of the Smoke-free Premises and Vehicles (Wales) Regulations 2020, was used in the course of paid or voluntary work with there being more than one person present in the vehicle, one of whom was present for the purpose of receiving goods or services from the person using the vehicle, failed to take reasonable steps to cause a person, namely **(..SPECIFY PERSON SMOKING..), smoking in that vehicle to stop smoking
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 15(1) and (3)(a) and 17 of the Smoke-free Premises and Vehicles (Wales) Regulations 2020 and sections 6(5)(c), (6) and (9) and 15 of the Public Health (Wales) Act 2017.

english.notes:
(i) Smoke-free vehicles are defined in regulation 15 of the Smoke-free Premises and Vehicles (Wales) Regulations 2020. Vehicles which are smoke-free by virtue of paragraph (3) are smoke-free only when the vehicle is being used as described in that paragraph.
(ii) Where the vehicle is used wholly or mainly in the course of paid or voluntary work and by more than one person or to transport members of the public, see H22454/PH17011; where it is used for private purposes and a child is present, see H22456/PH17013.
(iii) For a defence where the person did not know, and could not reasonably have been expected to know, that the person in question was smoking, see section 6(7) and (8) of the Public Health (Wales) Act 2017.
